  "text": "The laundromat on Bell Street had one machine nobody used.

Its door was taped shut. A handwritten sign read: FOUND CLOTHES ONLY.

On Tuesdays, I watched the owner feed it single socks, forgotten scarves, gloves stiff from the gutter. He never added detergent.

One evening, I brought him my father's coat.

“Is he missing?” he asked.

“Dead.”

“That's different.”

He pushed the coat back across the counter.

I returned after closing. The side window had a broken latch, something my father would have noticed and repaired without being asked.

I put his coat in the machine and found a quarter beneath the radiator.

The drum turned once.

From inside came the sound of keys landing in a bowl.

Then a cough.

My father had coughed like that for twenty years, softly, almost apologetically.

I knelt beside the door.

“Dad?”

A hand pressed against the glass. His wedding ring clicked against it.

Behind me, the owner switched on the lights.

“Don't open it.”

“He's in there.”

“Yes,” he said. “But where did you think the missing clothes went?”

Something red drifted past the hand. A child's mitten. Then another. Scarves wound around an elbow. Sleeves pulled tight across shoulders I could not see.

My father's voice asked me to hurry.

The owner unplugged the machine.

We sat until morning, listening to the handle rattle.

When it finally stopped, he peeled away the tape and opened the door.

The coat lay inside, neatly folded.

In its pocket were my father's keys.

I took them home. I didn't think about the key to my apartment until I heard it turn in the lock."
